_about: Manual review, for the run in results/lib367-sonnet.json, of questions that the judge majority marks wrong AND that Mafin2.5's human reviewers labeled BE (benchmark error), MVA (multiple valid approaches) or SEDC (same evidence, different conclusion). Such a question counts as correct only when our answer reaches the same conclusion as Mafin2.5's reviewed answer (agrees_with_mafin). Reviewed by the coding agent that ran the evaluation, not by a financial expert; the notes say what was compared. answer_sha1 is the first 12 hex digits of the SHA-1 of the reviewed answer; adjudicate.ts refuses an entry whose answer changed.

financebench_id_00585.note: Reports the 10-K's own effective tax rates, (0.6)% for FY2022 and 14.8% for FY2021, as Mafin2.5 did; the gold answer has the signs reversed.

financebench_id_00005.note: Working capital of $2,278M from total current assets and liabilities, the same figure as Mafin2.5; the gold answer uses an operating-items subset ($831M). All three say it is positive.

financebench_id_00790.note: Concludes CVS is not capital-intensive from capex/revenue and PP&E/assets, as Mafin2.5 did; the gold answer says it is, from a low return on assets.

financebench_id_01911.note: Mafin2.5 subtracted rent and D&A from Adjusted EBITDAR and got a negative Adjusted EBIT (-3.25x coverage). Our agent left out rent and got +$15M and 0.03x. Counted wrong.

financebench_id_00080.note: Working capital of about $12.4B with the caveat that customer funds dominate both sides, the same figure and caveat as Mafin2.5; the gold answer says $1.6B.

financebench_id_00283.note: The agent read Pfizer's 2019 10-K instead of the Q2 2023 10-Q and answered about $355M; Mafin2.5 answered $70M from the 10-Q. Counted wrong.

financebench_id_02419.note: No spin-off in progress as of Q2 2023 because the Upjohn separation closed in 2020, the same conclusion as Mafin2.5; the gold answer says Upjohn is being spun off.
